Package neqsim.thermo.characterization

Class OilAssayCharacterisation

java.lang.Object
neqsim.thermo.characterization.OilAssayCharacterisation
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Cloneable
public class OilAssayCharacterisation extends Object implements Cloneable, Serializable
Utility for characterising an oil system from refinery-assay cut information.

An assay is represented as a set of pre-binned cuts on one declared composition basis: all cuts must use either mass fractions or volume fractions. Volume-basis cuts are converted to a mass basis with the cut densities before moles are calculated. Mixing mass- and volume-basis cuts in one assay is rejected because the missing conversion basis would otherwise be ambiguous.

Molar masses are in kg/mol throughout this class. Density inputs used for petroleum characterisation are specific gravity (numerically equivalent to g/cm3 for the supported correlations); explicit kg/m3 input helpers are also provided.

Optional total-sulfur and total-nitrogen qualities are stored as mass fractions. Bulk qualities are reconstructed by linear mass-basis mixing rules after the assay basis has been resolved.

The TBP cut-boundary helpers preserve cut yields and boiling ranges, then use the midpoint of each boiling interval as the representative boiling point for the existing NeqSim petroleum correlation. They do not convert ASTM D86/D1160 or other laboratory distillation methods to TBP.

    • calculatePianoMolarMassKgPerMol

      public static double calculatePianoMolarMassKgPerMol(OilAssayCharacterisation.PianoHydrocarbonFamily[] families, int[] carbonNumbers, double[] massPercent)
      Calculate the number-average molar mass represented by PIANO mass-percent lumps.

      Each entry is defined by a hydrocarbon family, carbon number, and mass percentage. Ideal family formulas are used: paraffins and iso-paraffins are CnH(2n+2), naphthenes are CnH(2n), and aromatics are CnH(2n-6). The calculation uses conventional atomic weights C = 12.011 g/mol and H = 1.008 g/mol and returns the mixture number-average molar mass from the reciprocal mass-weighted sum. Percentages may differ from 100 by at most 0.1 percentage point to accommodate source-table rounding and are normalized by their actual sum.

      Parameters:
      families - PIANO hydrocarbon family for each lump
      carbonNumbers - carbon number for each lump
      massPercent - mass percentage for each lump
      Returns:
      number-average molar mass in kg/mol

    • addTBPCutBoundariesCelsius

      public void addTBPCutBoundariesCelsius(String namePrefix, double[] cumulativeVolumePercent, double[] boilingPointCelsius, double[] specificGravity)
      Add pre-binned true-boiling-point cuts from cumulative volume-percent boundaries.

      The first cumulative point must be 0 vol% and the last must be 100 vol%. The arrays of cumulative yield and boiling-point boundaries must have the same length. One specific gravity is required for each resulting interval. The interval midpoint is retained as the representative boiling point and the complete lower/upper boiling range is stored on the generated OilAssayCharacterisation.AssayCut.

      Parameters:
      namePrefix - component-name prefix; generated names are prefix + 1, prefix + 2, ...
      cumulativeVolumePercent - cumulative liquid-volume yield in percent, from 0 to 100
      boilingPointCelsius - TBP cut boundaries in degC
      specificGravity - specific gravity for each interval

    • getBulkSpecificGravity

      public double getBulkSpecificGravity()
      Reconstruct the bulk assay specific gravity from the configured cut yields and densities.

      The calculation uses ideal additive liquid volumes. For resolved cut mass fractions w_i and cut specific gravities SG_i, the bulk value is 1 / sum(w_i / SG_i). The same expression is used for mass- and liquid-volume-basis assays after the existing basis and closure validation has been applied. No thermodynamic component is created or modified.

      This is a screening property at the density reference conditions represented by the cut inputs. It does not apply temperature correction, excess-volume, or blend-contraction models.

      Returns:
      reconstructed dimensionless bulk specific gravity
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the assay is empty, incomplete, mixed-basis, or lacks a cut density

    • getBulkDensityKgPerCubicMetreAt60F

      public double getBulkDensityKgPerCubicMetreAt60F()
      Reconstruct the bulk assay density at 60 degF from getBulkSpecificGravity().

      This method keeps dimensionless specific gravity separate from physical density. It uses a water density of 999.016 kg/m3 at 60 degF and inherits the ideal-additive-volume assumptions and validation boundary of getBulkSpecificGravity().

      Returns:
      reconstructed bulk density at 60 degF in kg/m3
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if bulk specific gravity cannot be reconstructed

    • getBulkSulfurMassFraction

      public double getBulkSulfurMassFraction()
      Reconstruct the bulk assay total-sulfur mass fraction from assay-cut sulfur data.

      The calculation is the linear mass-basis mixing rule sum(w_i S_i), where w_i are the resolved assay mass fractions and S_i are cut sulfur mass fractions. Volume-basis assays therefore use the same density-based conversion as getResolvedMassFractions(). Every positive-yield cut must define sulfur; zero-yield cuts do not contribute.

      Returns:
      bulk total-sulfur mass fraction on a 0-1 basis
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the assay is empty, incomplete, mixed-basis, or lacks sulfur data for a positive-yield cut

    • apply

      public void apply()
      Generate TBP pseudo-components for all configured cuts and add them to the attached system.

      All inputs are resolved and validated before the first pseudo-component is added. Existing component names are rejected so that repeated calls cannot silently double the assay.
